```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Many genetic analyses require a set of unrelated individuals. RedKinNet selects one from
pairwise kinship estimates: pairs related above a threshold form a network, each connected
component of the network is a family, and a set of unrelated individuals of the largest
possible size, a *maximum set*, is chosen family by family. This vignette goes through the
whole workflow on the example cohort shipped with the package; the vignettes
*Selecting with covariates* and *Selection uncertainty* cover the other ways of choosing.

```{r}
library(RedKinNet)
```

## The example cohort

`rkn_example` is a synthetic cohort of `r nrow(rkn_example$samples)` samples. Its kinship
table lists the pairs with an estimated kinship of at least 0.02, as written by KING or by
PLINK 2 with a minimum kinship; the samples without relatives appear in no row, so their
identifiers come from a separate table, which also holds the covariates.

```{r}
kin <- rkn_example$kinship
covariates <- rkn_example$samples
head(kin)
head(covariates)
```

## Checking the samples

Before selecting, `rkn_check_samples()` looks for samples that distort the network: pairs
with a kinship above 0.354, possible duplicates or monozygotic twins, and samples related to
unusually many others, a sign of contamination of the DNA sample.

```{r}
chk <- rkn_check_samples(kin, threshold = "third", samples = covariates$id)
chk
```

The contaminated sample is related to most of the cohort and holds hundreds of samples in a
single family; without it, the largest family is much smaller. The duplicated pair needs no
action for the selection, which keeps at most one of the two samples, but it deserves a
quality check.

## Building the network

`rkn_graph_from_kinship()` joins the samples whose kinship reaches the threshold. The
threshold is a number or the name of a degree of relationship, `"duplicate"`, `"first"`,
`"second"` or `"third"`, for the corresponding KING cutoff; `"third"` joins relatives up to
first cousins. The contaminated sample is excluded, and the covariates become vertex
attributes. Since the samples were checked above, `check = FALSE` skips the check that the
function would otherwise run.

```{r}
g <- rkn_graph_from_kinship(kin, threshold = "third", samples = covariates$id,
                            exclude = chk$contamination$id, covariates = covariates,
                            check = FALSE)
g
table(igraph::components(g)$csize)
```

Most samples have no relatives, and they are always selected; the families with two or more
members are those where a choice has to be made.

## Selecting unrelated individuals

`rkn_select_random()` returns a maximum set: within each family, structural rules keep or
discard the members whose fate is the same in the maximum sets they consider, and the
remaining choices are made at random. A seed makes the selection reproducible.

```{r}
sel <- rkn_select_random(g, seed = 1)
sel
head(sel$kept)
```

With `uniform = TRUE`, each family is resolved by an exact algorithm that draws one of all
its maximum sets with equal probability; the rules of the default selection never choose some
of the maximum sets of larger families.

```{r}
sel_uniform <- rkn_select_random(g, uniform = TRUE, seed = 1)
sel_uniform
```

The printed summary reports how many maximum sets the network has and how much two uniform
draws differ on average: the selection is one of many equally valid ones. The vignette
*Selection uncertainty* shows how to quantify the consequences.

## Diagnostics

Each selection records how every individual was decided (`node_diagnostics`) and how every
family was resolved (`family_summary`).

```{r}
head(sel$node_diagnostics[, c("id", "pre_class", "post_class", "family_id", "family_size")])
summary(sel)
```

The plots draw the families with the selected and discarded individuals; `min_family_size`
leaves out the smallest families.

```{r, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
plot(sel, min_family_size = 6)
```

## Saving the selection

The selected identifiers can be written to a file for downstream tools, for instance as a
list of samples to keep in PLINK.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
writeLines(sel$kept, "unrelated_samples.txt")
```
